challenges.name: cookie-flags-quiz
challenges.title: Which requests carry the refresh cookie?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the cookie incident: the refresh cookie that reached a learner preview app, and a logout response whose clearing cookie did not clear anything.

questions.question: Sign-in response from https://api.codedev.test (before the fix): Set-Cookie: cd_rt=rt_K7mQ2v...; Max-Age=2592000; Domain=codedev.test; Path=/auth/refresh; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict Learner preview apps run learner-written server code at https://.preview.codedev.test. The preview page of u-4821 contains: Statement: "Because the cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and limited to Path=/auth/refresh, a signed-in learner who opens this preview page does not send cd_rt to the preview app's server."
questions.explanation: False. Domain=codedev.test makes the cookie match every host under codedev.test (RFC 6265, section 5.1.3 domain-match), including u-4821.preview.codedev.test. Path only compares the request path, and the image requests exactly /auth/refresh on that host, so the path matches too. SameSite=Strict does not help: the preview page and the cookie's host share the registrable domain codedev.test, so the request is same-site. HttpOnly only hides the cookie from JavaScript; the browser still puts it in the Cookie header, where the learner's server code can log it. The fix is a host-only cookie (no Domain attribute), which RFC 6265 sends only to api.codedev.test. The misconception is that HttpOnly, Strict and Path together form a boundary; each one limits something different, and none of them limits the host.

questions.question:
Sign-in set:

Set-Cookie: __Secure-cd_rt=rt_9Lp...; Max-Age=2592000; Expires=Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:00:00 GMT; Path=/auth/refresh; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

The logout handler calls res.clearCookie("__Secure-cd_rt", { secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: "strict" }) and the response contains:

Set-Cookie: __Secure-cd_rt=; Path=/; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict

DevTools > Application > Cookies after logout still lists __Secure-cd_rt with Path /auth/refresh and the old value.

Statement: "The refresh cookie survived logout because the clearing cookie had a different Path, so the browser treated it as a different cookie."
questions.explanation: True. A browser identifies a stored cookie by its name, domain and path (RFC 6265, section 5.3, step 11): a new Set-Cookie replaces an old cookie only when all three match. The clearing header has Path=/ (the default of clearCookie when no path is passed), so it describes a different cookie that is already expired and is simply not stored, while the cookie with Path=/auth/refresh keeps its value until it expires. The fix is to clear with exactly the attributes it was set with: the same name, the same Path and the same Domain (or no Domain). The misconception is that a cookie is identified by its name alone.

challenges.name: auth-cookie-headers
challenges.title: Build the auth cookie headers
challenges.description: CodeDev's refresh cookie was set with Domain=codedev.test, so browsers sent it to every subdomain, including learner preview apps that run learner-written server code. Write buildAuthCookies(config, nowMs, accessToken, refreshToken), which returns the exact Set-Cookie values for sign-in and logout. Secure goes on every cookie unless config.environment is "local-http" (a documented dev mode for plain http://), where no cookie gets it. Validate first and return { ok: false, error } for the first failing rule, in this order: "invalid ttl" (accessTtlSeconds and refreshTtlSeconds are not both whole numbers >= 1, or refresh <= access); "invalid refresh path" (refreshPath does not match /^\/[A-Za-z0-9\/_-]+$/); "SameSite=None requires Secure"; "cookie prefix requires Secure" (a name starting with __Host- or __Secure- without Secure); "__Host- cookie must not have Domain" (a __Host- name while domain is not null); "__Host- cookie requires Path=/" (refreshName starts with __Host-); "invalid token value" (a token that does not match /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/). Otherwise return { ok: true, login: [access, refresh], logout: [clearAccess, clearRefresh] }. Each value uses this attribute order joined by "; ": <name>=<value>; Max-Age=<seconds>; Expires=<date>[; Domain=<domain>]; Path=<path>[; Secure]; HttpOnly; SameSite=<value>. The access cookie uses accessName, Path=/ and config.sameSite; the refresh cookie uses refreshName, Path=refreshPath and always SameSite=Strict. Expires is new Date(nowMs + ttlSeconds * 1000).toUTCString() on the fake clock nowMs. Domain appears only when config.domain is not null. A clearing cookie has the same name, an empty value, Max-Age=0, Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT and the same Domain, Path, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite as the cookie it clears. The test runner reads { cases: [{ config, nowMs, accessToken, refreshToken }] } as JSON and prints the array of results.
hints: Which single boolean decides whether Secure appears, and which validation rules depend on it? And for logout: what must a clearing cookie share with the cookie it clears for the browser to treat it as the same cookie?

Look at three places: the validation order (return the first rule that fails; check prefixes with startsWith on both names), one header builder used for all four values (collect the parts in an array, add Domain and Secure only when they apply, then join with "; "), and the units (Max-Age is in seconds, Date and nowMs are in milliseconds; toUTCString() already prints the Expires format).

A similar cookie on other input: a language cookie named lang with value vi, ttl 3600 s, Path=/, SameSite=Lax, no Domain, in local-http mode at nowMs 0 gives "lang=vi; Max-Age=3600; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 01:00:00 GMT; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax", and its clearing value is "lang=; Max-Age=0; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax". Renamed __Host-lang with Domain=codedev.test in production, the same config is rejected before any header is built.
